papers.title: High-Throughput Private Information Retrieval with on-CPU Accelerators
papers.abstract: We present AltoPIR, the first PIR system that exploits the capability of emerging on-CPU matrix accelerators such as Intel AMX. Unlike existing solutions, AltoPIR achieves high-performance PIR through efficient batching without requiring discrete accelerators. However, the on-CPU accelerator has only a few small registers and shares its core with request handling. As a result, it runs far below its peak rate while its operands arrive from memory, and it remains idle while its core handles requests. To keep the accelerator busy, we design mechanisms that reduce both the memory traffic of a batch and the core cycles spent on each request. Our experimental results show that AltoPIR outperforms existing CPU-based solutions by up to 50.1x.

papers.title: TripleKV: Predict, Prefetch, Protect - KV Cache Management for AI Agents
papers.abstract: LLM agents alternate between inference and tool execution, repeatedly reusing their growing context across calls. Under high concurrency, their combined key-value (KV) cache working set can reach hundreds of GiB, far exceeding GPU memory capacity. As idle KV cache blocks are evicted to slower storage tiers, returning agents incur expensive retrievals that stall inference. To address this problem, we present TripleKV, a three-tier KV cache management system that hides the delays of these retrievals. In agentic workloads, the KV blocks needed by the next inference request are known in advance; only the time of their reuse is uncertain. TripleKV uses a tool-aware latency predictor to estimate when each tool call will complete and prefetches the required KV blocks from SSD into host DRAM ahead of time. Unlike GPU prefetching, this avoids reserving scarce GPU memory and interfering with concurrent inference requests. To further improve DRAM utilization, TripleKV eliminates duplication of GPU-resident blocks in DRAM, and introduces a victim-cache mechanism that refills blocks from SSD upon their eviction from GPU memory. Across data, web, and coding agents, TripleKV reduces the fraction of requests requiring critical-path SSD reads from 45-76% to under 10%. It also reduces P95 time to first token (TTFT) by up to 49% compared with vLLM extended with DRAM and SSD KV-cache tiers, and achieves 1.5-7$\times$ lower P95 TTFT than recent agent-aware systems.

papers.title: Ossim: OS-Driven Live Simulation for Cluster-Scale Full-Stack Evaluation (Extended Version)
papers.abstract: Cluster-scale full-stack simulation is essential for evaluating distributed software stacks and emerging hardware components before deployment. Such simulation must achieve both full-stack fidelity for the unmodified production stack and the simulation performance required for iterative configuration exploration. However, no existing method achieves both. We present Ossim, an OS-level approach to cluster-scale full-stack simulation built on top of the Linux virtualization stack. Ossim comprises four subsystems: simulation-oriented scheduling, live memory hierarchy management, simulation-aware IPC, and multi-host coordination. Together, they coordinate live and modeled components under shared simulated time while controlling interference among co-located live VMs. These mechanisms point toward simulation-native OS support, where simulation control and orchestration become core OS responsibilities.

papers.title: Compact Two-dimensional RAID Level 6 Arrays Tolerating Quadruple Node Failures
papers.abstract: We investigate the first two-dimensional RAID arrays tolerating quadruple failures. These arrays start with n RAID level 6 parity stripes with two parity nodes per stripe. Our study shows that these arrays experience between 87 and 99.99 percent fewer fatal quintuple failures and between 77 and 99.98 fewer fatal sextuple failures than multiple n-out-of-n+k arrays with the same storage capacity and the same space overhead. In addition, adding two superparity nodes to the array eliminates all fatal quintuple failures and 85 percent of all sextuple failures.

papers.title: TideSand: Performance-Accurate Sandbox Multiplexing for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: We propose TideSand, a sandbox system that intelligently multiplexes resources for performance-sensitive LLM agents, such as auto research agents working on system measurement tasks. TideSand combines three key ideas: agent-aware scheduling, which schedules sandbox execution intelligently at the tool call level to avoid resource contention; speculative swapping, which offloads the memory of sandboxes waiting on inference and restores it before their next tool call; and selective rollback, which checkpoints selected sandboxes when contention occurs and restores them when machines are idle. We evaluate TideSand across six model-workload pairs on AlgoTune, Terminal-Bench 4.0, and Terminal-Bench Science. TideSand achieves 3.8-10x higher throughput than strict reservation while maintaining tool-call fidelity, or 7-44% higher fidelity than overcommit baselines at similar throughput. Moreover, TideSand reduces the evaluation error on Algotune by 19x through improved tool-call fidelity. We hope the work motivates future research to maintain tool call fidelity while keeping resource utilization high through statistical multiplexing.
